title: Grid-connected LFP battery storage system
description:
Design a grid-connected lithium iron phosphate battery energy storage system for a site in Germany. Requirements at the point of connection to the 10 kV network: usable energy 4 MWh and rated power 2 MW (charge and discharge, 2 h duration) over a service life of 10 years. Apply the NASA Systems Engineering Handbook technical margin policy at CDR: 15% on energy and 15% on power. End of life is 80% state of health. Usable energy follows the PNNL ESGC 2022 definitions (SOC window, state of health, and the DC, PCS and transformer efficiencies between cells and the point of connection; DC-side one-way efficiency 0.954).

Architecture: one string per rack; every string connects to its own DC input on a PCS unit (no combiner boxes; a PCS unit's inputs share one DC bus, and the PCS units are paralleled on the AC side); cells in series in modules of 16 (the series count is a multiple of 16). Each string has one fuse and one contactor and runs to the PCS over one DC cable pair (optionally several pairs in parallel) of 60 m route length, with 6 strings sharing each cable tray. DC circuit time constant L/R 2 ms. DC cable voltage drop limit 1.5%.

Site: maximum ambient 35 C, annual mean 12 C, altitude 200 m; cable ambient inside the enclosure 35 C.

Cell (LFP prismatic): 3.2 V nominal, 280 Ah, 2.5-3.65 V, DC resistance 0.52 mOhm at beginning of life growing by a factor 1.96 at end of life, continuous 0.5 C charge and discharge, operating SOC window 5-95%, open-circuit voltage 3.07 V at 5% SOC, maximum cell temperature 55 C, price 67.63 per cell.

Design rules to apply, by name: string voltage window against the PCS DC window at end of life; PCS output at site ambient per the catalog columns; cooling at site ambient; string fuse selection per IEC 60269-7 (battery fuse class, DC voltage rating at the circuit time constant, ambient factor from the catalog, continuous-load factor 0.8, breaking capacity against the prospective fault current at the DC bus per IEC 61660-1 with the PCS contribution from the catalog); contactor coordination with the fuse (no interruption gap); DC cable current-carrying capacity per DIN VDE 0298-4 with the temperature and grouping factors below and overload coordination per IEC 60364-4-43 (DIN VDE 0100-430); reactive power capability at the point of connection per VDE-AR-N 4110 (cos phi 0.95 under- and over-excited) including the transformer's own reactive consumption from its short-circuit impedance; transformer rating per IEC 60076-11 with the annual-mean ambient factors below.

NASA/SP-2016-6105-SUPPL Expanded Guidance for NASA SE, sec. 7.8 (public domain): technical margin policy by milestone
IEC 60269-7 battery fuses as described in SIBA, Mersen and ETI battery-fuse catalogs: gBat/aBat, DC rating at time constant, ambient factors, breaking capacity
IEC 61660-1 DC short-circuit method as described in ABB 1SDC007104G0201 Annex B: battery branch peak and quasi-steady current
DIN VDE 0298-4 / IEC 60364-5-52 current-carrying capacity and IEC 60364-4-43 overload coordination as reproduced in ABB 2CDC401002D0106 and Mersen EduPack TM-104
Eaton 'Five factors' OCPD note: fuse and contactor interruption coordination (no gap)
VDE-AR-N 4110 reactive power requirement at the connection point as stated in TEN / Nordhausen Netz TAR-MS guidelines and VDE FNN Hinweis Speicher
IEC 60076-11 dry-type transformer rated conditions and annual-mean ambient factors as stated in Siemens GEAFOL planning notes
